title: Collect light with a wider lens
hook: Change aperture diameter and predict collected power.
misconception: collected power doubles when aperture diameter doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply P ∝ aperture area ∝ D² to compare collected power when aperture diameter changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a uniformly illuminated unobstructed circular aperture with fixed irradiance, P ∝ aperture area ∝ D². When aperture diameter doubles, collected power becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model P ∝ aperture area ∝ D²; scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a uniformly illuminated unobstructed circular aperture with fixed irradiance, with a nonzero initial result. If aperture diameter triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on collected power?
recall.why: Apply P ∝ aperture area ∝ D² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
